Factory-built skids

Factory-integrated frames, piping, CDU, cable pathways and containment. Transport splits and site connections planned before fabrication, so the field scope is countable.

One of the most effective ways to reduce leak risk is to make fewer joints in the field. A skid moves the CDU, pumps, balancing and isolation valves, filtration, sample ports and controls into a factory where each boundary can be pressure-tested, flushed to a cleanliness class and released against written criteria, with the record attached to the serial.

We design the skid around the project's acceptance criteria, including the transport splits and site connections, and have it built by manufacturing partners we have qualified. We own the specification and the factory acceptance test, and we are accountable for how the skid performs in the line within the agreed scope and acceptance criteria.

Specification and interfaces

The fields buyers compare. Values depend on the configuration, so we do not publish one set of numbers; each project gets a data sheet with every row filled in at stated conditions.

FieldHow it is statedValue
Rated heat load and rating conditionskW at stated supply temperatures, approach and fluid, for the skid as a wholeConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Equipment on the skidCDU, pumps, filtration, valves, sample ports, sensors and controls, listedConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Primary and secondary flow and pressure dropFlow at rated load and pressure drop or available pressure on each loopConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Pump redundancyN, N+1 or 2N, and how a pump is isolated for serviceConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Maximum allowable working pressureFor each loop, with the factory test pressureConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Wetted materials and coolant compatibilityNamed materials per loop; fluids and glycol concentrations allowedConfigured per project; data sheet on request
FiltrationFull-flow rating and its basis; side-stream filtration if fittedConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Transport splitsNumber of shipping sections, and the size and weight of the largestConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Site connectionsCount of pipe, power and control connections made on site, each with its testConfigured per project; data sheet on request
FAT checklistTests run before release, with acceptance criteria (see the FAT record template)Configured per project; data sheet on request
Installation conditionsFloor loading, footprint, levelling, access route and lifting pointsConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Interfaces and communicationsPipe connection type and size; control and monitoring protocols; signals to the building systemsConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Dimensions, weight and service clearancesPer section and assembled; access needed for maintenanceConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Supply boundaryWhat we supply and what the site contractor provides, drawn at each connectionConfigured per project; data sheet on request
Request the data sheetSee the FAT record template
What we ask the project to decide early
  • FAT protocol agreed before build
  • Cleanliness class stated and sampled
  • Field connections limited to flanges with a test plan
